I can't tell you whether to buy or rent. That depends on your income, savings, down payment, time horizon and risk tolerance, and it is personal financial advice, which I can't give. Here are the Toronto figures I could retrieve, which may help you frame the decision.

1. New home prices (Toronto, total house and land, index 2016=100), table 18-10-0205: 110.4 in 2025-09 and 105.0 in 2026-09. Change: (105.0 − 110.4) / 110.4 = −4.9%. This covers newly built homes only, not resale, and is an index rather than a dollar price.

2. Average rent (CMHC, Toronto, two-bedroom units in row and apartment structures of three or more units), table 34-10-0133: $1,972 in 2024-01 and $2,045 in 2025-01. Change: (2,045 − 1,972) / 1,972 = +3.7%. The latest figure available in this table is the 2025-01 survey, which is older than the new-home data.

Not covered: resale home prices, mortgage rates, property taxes, condo fees, and the cost of buying versus renting over time. My tools did not return these, so I can't compare them. A financial adviser or a mortgage broker can help with the rest.
